Solar Energy: An Overview
Solar energy harnesses the radiant light and heat from the Sun using technologies like photovoltaic (PV) panels and solar thermal collectors. It is one of the fastest-growing sources of renewable electricity. Photovoltaic cells convert sunlight into electricity through the photovoltaic effect, first observed by Edmond Becquerel in 1839. Commercial silicon panels have an efficiency of about 20 to 23 percent, while laboratory cells can exceed 45 percent. The cost of solar modules has fallen by roughly 90 percent between 2010 and 2020 due to mass production, improved manufacturing, and economies of scale. The main challenges of solar power include intermittency, where panels produce no electricity at night and less on cloudy days, and land use for large solar farms. Battery storage systems and rooftop installations, as well as agrivoltaics, help mitigate these issues.
